Abstract. The origin of biological rhythms—from the heartbeat to circadian cycles—
remains an open question in systems biology. Denis Noble has argued that the genome
does not encode a "master clock," yet organisms exhibit coherent periodicities. We
propose that these rhythms are rooted in a fundamental inertial resonance of matter itself.
The Universal Particle Principle (UPP) derives a 1-second timescale from the proton's
geometry, linking quantum chromodynamics, gravitation, and the fine structure constant.
Independently, the Geesink–Meijer (GM) Acoustic Quantum Code reveals a discrete 12-
band spectrum, normalized by octaves, in which the proton appears at 1.5 Hz and 1.333
seconds per cycle—the harmonic ratios 3/2 and 4/3. We show that the GM scale is self-
dual under octave-normalized reciprocation: its twelve invariants form six pairs, each
pair multiplying to one octave (2). The proton's position at 3/2 therefore implies its
position at 4/3, because 4/3 is the octave-normalized reciprocal of 3/2. The factor 3 in the
frequency ratio reflects the proton's three valence quarks; the factor 4/3 is a structural
consequence of the scale's self-duality, not an independent empirical fact. Extending to
genetics, Pythagorean ratios such as 3/2 appear in molecular parameters of the genetic
code (Petoukhov & Boulay). We further introduce the Octave Rule, showing that the mass
gap and the four fundamental force couplings, when octave scaled, map onto the 12-band
GM spectrum. We thus propose a unified framework in which the proton acts as a
geometric clock, the GM scale as its harmonic spectrum, the Octave Rule as its universal
normalization principle, and the genetic code as its biochemical readout. The framework
yields testable predictions for exoplanetary architectures, chronobiology, and
mitochondrial dynamics.
1. Introduction
The question of biological timing has long resisted reduction to the genome. Denis Noble
has forcefully argued that the gene centric view of evolution is insufficient, pointing to
the heart as a prime example: there is no genetic "instruction" that specifies the rhythm of
the heartbeat, nor is there a master clock in the DNA. Yet the heart beats with a robust
periodicity of approximately one second, and organisms across scales exhibit coherent
oscillations—from circadian ( h) to ultradian (minutes to hours) to millisecond ion
channel dynamics.
In parallel, quantum physics has shown that matter possesses intrinsic periodicities. De
Broglie (1924) associated to every massive particle an internal period .
His words and postulate: "The fundamental assumption of existence of a certain periodic
phenomenon of a yet to be determined character, which is to be attributed to each isolated
energy parcel [elementary particle]"; and is called the "de Broglie internal clock" (see
Figure 1).
Figure 1. Louis-Victor de Broglie (1929)
Penrose (2011): "For there is a clear sense in which any individual stable massive particle
plays a role as a virtually perfect clock. Any stable massive particle behaves as a very
precise quantum clock, which ticks away with [Compton periodicity]."
Elementary cycles theory (ECT) postulates that every elementary "particle" of nature is
characterized by a persistent intrinsic spacetime periodicity. In ECT the Planck energy
spectrum is interpreted as a harmonic like spectrum of a massless periodic modalities of
fundamental time periodicity (Dolce, 2026).
However, for elementary particles this period is far too short to be biologically relevant.
The central insight of this paper is that the proton's geometry amplifies this quantum
period to the human scale second, and that this resonance manifests as a discrete acoustic
spectral code that extends across physical and biological systems.

That is, 4/3 is the octave-normalized reciprocal of 3/2. Because the GM scale is self-dual,
the proton's occupation of the 3/2 position in the frequency spectrum necessarily places it
at the 4/3 position in the period spectrum. The two positions are the same fact, seen from
two sides of the octave.
This has a direct consequence for the interpretation of the ratios:
- The factor 3 in 3/2 reflects the proton's three valence quarks. It is an empirical and
structural fact about the proton's composition. The UPP's coupling contains
the same factor 3 for the same reason: the strong-force confinement volume scales with
the number of valence quarks.
- The factor 4/3 is not an independent empirical fact. It is a structural consequence of the
self-duality of the GM scale. Once the proton is located at 3/2, its position at 4/3 follows
automatically, and no additional physical input is required. The appearance of 4/3 in the
spectrum is therefore not a second coincidence to be explained; it is the same fact as the
3/2 position, expressed in the dual variable.
This distinction matters because it preempts a natural objection. One might argue that any
two numerical agreements can be manufactured by choosing enough parameters. In the
present case, the 3/2 and 4/3 positions are not two independent agreements; they are one
agreement viewed through the scale's symmetry. The counting of "coincidences" is
thereby reduced by one, and the remaining single agreement—the proton's position at the
eighth scalar—is the substantive claim.

4.4 The Harmonic Bridge, Stated Precisely
The harmonic bridge between the UPP and the GM model can now be stated cleanly.
The UPP side. The proton's geometry—its measured radius and mass, its three-quark
composition, and the fine-structure constant—predicts a fundamental inertial resonance at
corresponding to Hz. This resonance is the geometric eigenvalue of the proton,
mediated by the granularity of spacetime ( ) and the gravitational coupling ( ).
The GM side. The GM scale places the proton at 3/2 times the Higgs root frequency, and
—by self-duality—at 4/3 times the Higgs root period. The Higgs root is at 1 Hz.
The bridge. The UPP's 1 Hz resonance is the GM's Higgs root. The proton's position at
3/2 in the GM frequency spectrum is the acoustic expression of the same three-quark
structure that appears in the UPP's coupling . The factor 4/3 follows from
the scale's self-duality. The two frameworks therefore converge on the same one-second
anchor, with the UPP supplying the geometric reason for the anchor and the GM scale
supplying the empirical spectrum that confirms and extends it.
5. The Octave Rule: A Universal Normalization Principle
The octave rule formalizes the observation that nature's fundamental oscillators are
separated by factors of two. For any fundamental interaction or particle mass, its
characteristic energy or coupling constant, when converted to a frequency and normalized
by powers of two ( ), falls precisely onto one of the 12 GM scalars in the listening
window between 1 and 2 Hz. This is not a fitting exercise; it is a discovery. The GM scale
is not an arbitrary musical metaphor—it is a discrete eigenvalue spectrum of nature,
revealed by octave normalization.

5.1. The Mass Gap
In quantum field theory, the lowest possible energy state is the vacuum, which is
considered to be zero. A mass gap means the next possible energy state sits above zero by
a finite, positive amount ( ). The lower bound mass gap proves to be definitively
greater than zero ( ). A lower bound of 76 MeV acts as a conservative, analytically
derived mathematical floor—safely below the 135 MeV physical pion mass—based on
the principle that the strong force spectrum is strictly "gapped" and cannot feature
massless excitations.
When the octave rule is applied to the lower bound of 76 MeV, the delta is 0.84%; delta is
the percentual difference between 76 MeV and the energy calculated by the GM equation,
or called eigenstate. A difference lower than 1.60% between the measurement and the
scalar or the eigenfrequency calculated by the GM equation shows a high statistical
significance.
5.2. The Four Fundamental Force Couplings
The fundamental interactions or fundamental forces are interactions in nature that appear
not to be reducible to more basic interactions. There are four fundamental interactions
known to exist: electromagnetism, weak interaction, strong interaction and gravity. The
same octave rule can be applied to the four fundamental force couplings.

till 486 Hz and the scale between 1 Hz and 1.8984 Hz, respectively 2 Hz. For clarity,

(Geesink and Meijer, 2018).
Microtubules are cylindrical lattice polymers of the protein tubulin which organize
purposeful activities in brain neurons and all eukaryotic cells. Microtubules behave as
'fractal time crystals', characterized by self-similar resonance oscillations, 'clocks within
clocks' in a nested hierarchy of similar dynamics (‘triplet soft riplets') which repeat in
hertz, kilohertz, megahertz, gigahertz, and terahertz frequencies (Hameroff, 2026). The
measured and analyzed frequencies of microtubules correspond with the Acoustic
Quantum Code and a same energy distribution has been found for Bose-Einstein
condensates (Geesink and Schmieke, 2022).

NIR and MIR measurements of biological samples and water conformational states

mirror effect model of Tsenkova et al., 2009 could be further supported: mutual
cooperative oscillations exist in the spectra of water and biomolecules: vibrational modes
of molecules couple coherently.
J-resolved HMQC (Heteronuclear Multiple Quantum Coherence) and spin-echo NMR
experiments are able to measure proton-proton spin coupling constants at 2 and 3 Hz by
separating chemical shifts from scalar coupling interactions to reveal fine multiplet
structures (Furihata and Seto, 2001). Interestingly the proton resonance frequency of 400
MHz corresponds with an eigenfrequency of the GM-scalars.
9. Conclusion
We have shown that the proton's geometry defines a 1 Hz inertial resonance, and that this
resonance appears as the root of a discrete 12 band acoustic quantum spectrum. The
proton's position in that spectrum—at Hz and seconds per cycle—is geometrically
determined by its three valence quarks and spherical volume. The Octave Rule extends
this framework to the mass gap and the four fundamental force couplings, showing that
all fundamental constants of nature map onto the same 12band GM spectrum. The same
ratio appears in the genetic code, linking quantum geometry to molecular biology. This
cascade provides a physical answer to Denis Noble's question: the "master clock" is not
in the genome; it is in the geometry of matter itself, expressed through harmonic
resonances that span from the proton to the planet. The Biogenic hypothesis of the UPP
model and GM model could be further supported.
